name: Vehicle: Synchronized Journey beats duct-taped funnels
body: I just need better ads / a better funnel / a hotter offer — the tools I have are fine.
howWeHandleIt: The bottleneck isn't the tool, it's the lack of synchronized memory across channels. A Synchronized Journey makes a modest offer outperform a hot offer on duct tape.
proof: Case study: client went from 11% show-up to 38% show-up without changing ads, just by installing Lead State + state-based reminders.

name: External: Not-yet is not never
body: If they don't buy in the launch window, they're dead leads. I have to go get new ones.
howWeHandleIt: State-based follow-up and the Infinite Pipeline Loop turn every "not yet" into a future yes. Your highest-LTV clients are usually the ones who said no the first time.
proof: Data: 42% of converted clients in the last 12 months had said no on a prior event and re-entered via replay or nurture.

name: Internal: I'm capable of running a remembered pipeline
body: I'm not technical enough / my team isn't big enough / I always break automations.
howWeHandleIt: If a pipeline is modeled as Lead State, you don't maintain automations — you maintain one source of truth, and everything else reads from it. It's simpler, not more complex.
proof: Origin story: the moment I stopped rebuilding Zaps for every launch and started treating the lead as the database.
